question.problem:
The disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}⊔{A}_{4}$ of events ${A}_{1},{A}_{2},{A}_{3},{A}_{4}$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P({A}_{1}|B)$ given the following probabilities:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P(B|{A}_{1})=\frac{1}{5}, &  \\  & P(B|{A}_{2})=0, & P({A}_{2})=\frac{1}{4} \\  & P(B|{A}_{3})=\frac{1}{5}, & P({A}_{3})=\frac{1}{8} \\  & P(B|{A}_{4})=\frac{2}{5}, & P({A}_{4})=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If the disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔…⊔{A}_{n}$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

$$
P({A}_{k}|B)=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{P(B)}=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})}
$$

where $k=1,2,…,n.$

In our case, $n=4,$ and ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}⊔{A}_{4}$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

$$
P({A}_{1})+P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})+P({A}_{4})=1.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{1}) & =1-(P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})+P({A}_{4})) \\  & =1-(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{1}|B) & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{4}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})} \\  & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})}{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})+P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})+P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})+P(B|{A}_{4})P({A}_{4})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{5})(\frac{3}{8})}{(\frac{1}{5})(\frac{3}{8})+(0)(\frac{1}{4})+(\frac{1}{5})(\frac{1}{8})+(\frac{2}{5})(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{40})}{(\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
